---
title: "Software and Access Requirements"
description: "What MATH 346 students need, when they need it, and how to check it."
---

::: {.callout-important}
## The short version

You need **reliable access** to MATLAB for Weeks 1-5 and Project 1, and to R
for Weeks 6-15 and Project 2. Reliable access may be a verified laboratory
computer, an institutionally licensed online service, or your own computer. A
personal installation is recommended, but it is not a separate course
requirement if another reliable option is available outside scheduled class.
:::

## Requirement Matrix

| Software or service | Course use | Requirement | What the course provides |
|---|---|---|---|
| MATLAB | Weeks 1-5; Project 1 | **Required access** | Code examples, starter files, and a setup check |
| Symbolic Math Toolbox | Week 5 | **Required access for one teaching block** | Symbolic examples and a setup check; availability on the intended computer must be confirmed |
| R | Weeks 6-15; Project 2 | **Required access** | Code examples, starter files, and a setup check |
| RStudio Desktop or another instructor-approved R editor | Running and editing R scripts | **One R editor required**; RStudio is the recommended beginner option | In-class orientation uses the same basic script/console/files/plots workflow |
| `dplyr`, `ggplot2`, `readr`, `tidyr`, `stringr`, `lubridate` | Course R examples and Project 2 | **Required R packages** | The R setup check verifies all six |
| Quarto | Editing and rendering the supplied Week 6 report scaffold | **Required for the scaffolded Week 6 activity only** | A complete `.qmd` scaffold; students do not author a report from scratch |
| Word, Google Docs, or a compatible editor | Writing project reports | **One document editor required** | Editable project report templates |
| PDF export and a PDF reader | Both project submissions | **Required** | PDF is the readable report format |
| Current web browser, Blackboard access, and ZIP extraction | Materials, group files, and submission | **Required** | Group-specific ZIP packages and Blackboard submission instructions |
| Generative AI tool | Optional practice and permitted, documented project support | **Optional**; no paid AI account is required | Candidate AI answers are supplied when an activity needs one |
| Git and GitHub | Not used for student submission | **Optional** | The public course site can be used without Git |

Only access is required: students are not expected to purchase MATLAB,
Symbolic Math Toolbox, Microsoft Word, or an AI subscription. The instructor
will announce the verified institutional access routes before Week 1.

## Before Week 1: MATLAB

1. Open MATLAB on the computer you intend to use. This may be a local
   installation or [MATLAB Online](https://www.mathworks.com/products/matlab-online.html)
   if the institutional license provides the necessary access.
2. Download [the MATLAB setup check](../code/setup/check_matlab_setup.m).
3. In MATLAB, open the downloaded file and select **Run**.
4. Confirm that the output contains `MATLAB core check: PASS`.
5. Confirm before Week 5 that it also contains
   `Symbolic Math Toolbox check: PASS`.

If personal installation is the selected access route, use the
[official MathWorks installation instructions](https://www.mathworks.com/help/install/install-products.html)
and include Symbolic Math Toolbox. A basic MATLAB installation that does not
include that toolbox is insufficient for Week 5.

## Before Week 6: R and Quarto

Install in this order:

1. [R](https://cran.r-project.org/) itself;
2. [RStudio Desktop](https://posit.co/downloads) or another approved R editor;
3. [Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/get-started/);
4. the six required R packages.

Then download [the R setup check](../code/setup/check-r-setup.R), open it in
your R editor, and run the complete script. The final output must show:

- `R and required package check: PASS`; and
- `Quarto check: PASS`.

If packages are missing, the check prints the exact `install.packages(...)`
command to run. Quarto is used to render a supplied Week 6 scaffold; it is not
the required authoring format for either project.

## Project Reports

Both projects require:

- one PDF report created from the supplied Word/Google Docs-compatible
  template;
- executable MATLAB or R source code;
- the required machine-readable result files.

You do **not** need to write HTML or a project report in Quarto. See the
[project overview](../projects/index.qmd) for the complete submission contract.

## If Something Fails

Save the setup-check output or take a screenshot, record whether you used a
laboratory or personal computer, and contact the instructor before the relevant
week. Do not wait until a project deadline. The setup scripts test only small
temporary files and remove them when finished.
